output.brief:
The October night-premium errors were caused by a pay-rule change, not by your data. On 22 Oct an Ardentra consultant applied a template to rule NSP-02. It was logged as a label correction, but it also moved the premium window start from 20:00 to 22:00. The platform's audit trail records this, and no one can edit that trail. Internal audit recalculated pay for all 158 night workers. 147 were underpaid, and each shortfall equals the premium for the 20:00–22:00 hours. The 11 paid correctly work 22:00–06:00 shifts. In Ardentra's test tenant, setting the window back to 20:00 fixed all 158. Ardentra's claim about malformed shift codes doesn't hold up. Flagged staff were underpaid at a lower rate than unflagged staff. Release 7.4 and the bank file are not implicated. I'm quite sure of this.

Next steps:
1. Don't suspend the HR team, and don't re-cleanse and absorb the cost on Ardentra's say-so.
2. Have Ardentra restore the 20:00 start, verify it by re-running October, and pay all 147 underpaid staff off-cycle before 24 Nov.
3. Don't roll back 7.4.
4. Treat the overtime-cover drop as unresolved. The rota trial started in the same window, so the data can't separate the two causes. Keep the trial running for now and look at the reasons staff give.
5. Review the contract position on the change, since Ardentra's own change was mislabelled.
